lesson.title: Mission Control Retro-Burn Landing
lesson.buzzAssessmentTitle: Unit 1 Honors: Mission Control Retro-Burn Landing

gradingDesign.rule: All variable student evidence is graded only in the final two BusyBee responses.

questions.prompt: Burn displacement: How much height does the rocket gain from liftoff to engine cutoff? Enter meters.
What is the rocket's velocity at engine cutoff? Enter m/s.
How much additional height does the rocket gain from engine cutoff to the apex? Enter meters.
How long does the rocket coast from engine cutoff to the apex? Enter seconds.
What maximum height does the rocket reach above the pad? Enter meters.
How much time passes from liftoff to the apex? Enter seconds.
What is the total flight time from liftoff to touchdown across all four phases? Enter seconds.
What total distance does the rocket travel from liftoff to touchdown? Enter meters.
Explain why the rocket travels about 375 m but has approximately 0 m total displacement. Use the launch pad, apex, and touchdown positions in your explanation.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Distinguish total path length from final position minus initial position using the fixed mission.
a. Full credit: Explains that distance adds about 187.5 m upward and 187.5 m downward, while displacement is approximately zero because touchdown occurs at the starting pad.
  Partial credit: Correctly distinguishes distance and displacement but omits one mission value or does not clearly connect initial and final position.
  No credit: Treats distance and displacement as identical, reports negative distance, or gives no mission evidence.

questions.prompt: Analyze the complete rocket mission through powered burn, coast, free fall, and retro burn. For each phase, state what happens to velocity and acceleration, and use calculated values from at least two sections as evidence.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Address all four phases, distinguish velocity from acceleration, and cite at least two calculated mission values.
a. Full credit: Accurately analyzes velocity and acceleration in all four phases, notes that downward acceleration continues through coast and free fall even when velocity is zero at the apex, explains how retro acceleration reduces downward velocity for touchdown, and cites at least two correct calculated values.
  Partial credit: Correctly analyzes at least three phases and cites some evidence but omits a phase, confuses one sign, or provides only one calculated value.
  No credit: Gives no coherent phase analysis, claims acceleration is zero at the apex, or provides no calculated evidence.
